# Leveraging LLM-Generated Schema Descriptions for Unanswerable Question Detection in Clinical Data

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#sqd-schema-descriptions)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.706.pdf) · COLING 2025 proceedings, pages 10594-10601

**Reading coverage:** All eight PDF pages, Sections 1-6 and Appendices A-D; all tables and figure captions/associated explanation; Figure 4 visually inspected to recover rasterized examples.

## Research question

Direct answerability classifiers struggle with class imbalance, while generation-based uncertainty can require costly SQL models.

## Method

SQD generates descriptions from schema DDL, encodes each table description, and predicts question-table relevance using a T5-small encoder, learned prompt tokens and per-table heads. SQL-used tables provide supervision; a validation-selected maximum-score threshold decides answerability.

## Evaluation

EHRSQL-2024 supplies 5,124 training, 1,163 validation and 1,167 test questions over the same 17 tables. Comparisons include prompted LLMs, T5 binary classifiers, entropy filtering and ProbGate; unanswerable is the positive class.

## What the results support

The reported F1 is 0.8547 versus GPT-4o's 0.7778. Removing schema tokens or descriptions lowers performance. Appendix B illustrates correct relevance assignments and a false positive linked to the patients table.

## Limits and qualifications

New schemas and other domains are not evaluated. Table relevance may be high even when requested facts are unavailable, and the authors identify cases needing data exploration. Appendix D reports the best hyperparameter combination; the study does not validate downstream SQL correctness or clinical deployment.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Separates request screening from SQL generation and exposes limits of schema-only relevance for clinical answerability.
